To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the general linear model (a method for detecting phase-amplitude coupling in neural signals) is a good method for detecting phase amplitude coupling, but that it is not the only method.

(i) a general linear measure based on ESC is the best all round approach for detecting nested coupling in simulated and real ECoG data; (ii) the GLM measure can also detect nested coupling when the signal to noise level is high; (iii) the modulation index is a useful measure of nested coupling in real data, but not in simulation data; (iv) the PLV measure is not useful for detecting nested coupling.
the general linear model (a method for detecting nested oscillations in time series) is the most robust method for detecting nested rhythms in simulated data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether and how oscillations in the brain can be coupled to each other in a nested manner.
the question of what is the best way to detect nested oscillation.
the detection of nested oscillation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the modulation index is a good measure when the coupling is phase-locked, the PLV is a good measure of phase-locked coupling, the ESC and GLM are good measures of non-phase-locked coupling, but the ESC and GLMs are more reliable and robust than the PLV.
the GLM approach is the best all-around approach for detecting nested coupling in the presence of signal non-stationarity and/or multi-phasic coupling.
the GLM is a better measure of nested oscillation than the modulation index, but that it is not necessarily a better measure than PLV or ESC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GLM approach is robust, reliable, and easy to implement.
nested oscillation is a robust feature of brain activity, but it is not always easy to detect.
the best way to detect nested oscillations is to first use ESC to find a good candidate region, then to use the GLM measure to quantify the coupling strength in the candidate region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ESC is a powerful tool for investigating nested oscillations and that the GLM provides a simple way to use the ESC to detect nested oscillations.
, when testing for nested oscillation, it is essential to use an appropriate statistical measure that takes account of the non-stationarity of the data.
the GLMs are more sensitive than the PLV, and more robust to noise than either the modulation index or the ESC.
